newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU says housing for socially excluded a priority.
newsitem.headline: EU says housing for socially excluded a priority.

text.p: The EU said on Friday that providing housing for the homeless was a vital element in any integrated approach to tackling social exclusion across Europe.

"While housing is rarely seen as the single or, indeed, the prime factor underlying social exclusion, good quality housing can help prevent or alleviate the effects of social exclusion," Ireland's housing minister Liz McManus told a news conference after a two-day meeting of EU housing ministers.
Current EU president Ireland hosted the eighth annual informal meeting of EU housing ministers in Dublin based on the theme "Housing for Socially Excluded people".

"While the European Union does not have specific competence in the field of housing, these annual meetings provide a unique opportunity to exchange information ... on experiences and concepts in the area of housing policy," McManus said.

She said the meeting highlighted key issues in relation to the problem of social exclusion in a final communique by the ministers. It identified important pointers for the future direction of housing policy in tackling the problem of social exclusion.

"These included in particular physical renewal of housing, improved layout and design, greater social mix, better estate management, and more community involvement and tenant participation," McManus said.

She said the ministers agreed the effectiveness of action against social exclusion throughout the European Union can be significantly enhanced by co-operating in the exchange of ideas, experience and learning from different countries.
McManus said it was also agreed that particular emphasis should be placed on successful pilot or demonstration projects which are capable of being replicated in other member countries.

She said the meeting would help advance the effectiveness of policies to secure access to housing for the socially-excluded and the sharing of experiences, views and ideas "will make a significant contribution to informing our own policies and initiatives".
